biography.summary:
Julia Pianikova is a Russian violinist and a prizewinner of national and international competitions. She graduated with honours from the Central Music School of the Moscow State Tchaikovsky Conservatory and is currently a student at the Moscow Conservatory in the class of Professor Sergei Kravchenko, Honoured Artist of Russia.

She won First Prize at the 6th Kogan-Fest International Competition (Yaroslavl, 2025) and First Degree at the Igor Stravinsky International Competition (Moscow, 2023), and was a finalist at the Leonid Kogan International Competition (Brussels, 2021). As a member of a piano trio, she won the 26th Maria Yudina International Competition (Saint Petersburg, 2026), First Prize at the 3rd International Performing Arts Competition (Petrozavodsk, 2025), and became a laureate of the 8th Sergei Taneyev International Chamber Ensemble Competition (Moscow, 2025).

Julia has appeared at leading venues in Russia and abroad and has been invited to festivals and concerts as a soloist. She has performed with leading Russian symphony orchestras under conductors Mikhail Golikov, Filippo Dessi, Artem Markin, Vasily Valitov, Sergei Durygin and Dmitry Ralko.

She has repeatedly taken part in projects of the St Petersburg Music House, the Sirius Educational Centre and the All-Russian Youth Symphony Orchestra conducted by Yuri Bashmet. In 2023, Vadim Repin selected her for his master course at the Trans-Siberian Art Festival. She has been a scholarship recipient of the Soundout Foundation for Cultural and Educational Projects and Chamber Music since 2024.

Alongside her solo career, Julia is a co-founder of the Tellur Trio and a member of the early music ensemble Collegium musicum, which participates in the long-term project presenting all of J.S. Bach's cantatas at the Lutheran Cathedral of Saints Peter and Paul in Moscow.

## Baroque sonatas

Julia specialises in Baroque music in the tradition of historically informed performance. Her repertoire includes sonatas by Marini, Castello, Uccellini, Schmelzer, Pandolfi Mealli, Biber, Corelli, Rebel, Bach, Handel, Tartini, Leclair, Mondonville and others.

## Ensemble projects

Julia is a co-founder of the **Tellur Trio** and a member of other ensembles. The piano trio's programmes span Russian and international music from the 18th to the 21st century, with a particular interest in new Russian music and contemporary composers. She also performs with harpist Sofia Moskaleva and in other chamber formations.

projects.title: Tellur Trio
projects.description:
The ensemble's repertoire spans music from different eras, from the Viennese Classical school to the twentieth century. The trio gives particular prominence to contemporary classical music in its programmes.

The Tellur Trio presents concert programmes and music lectures at leading venues in Moscow and other Russian cities.

quotes.text: St Petersburg violinist Julia Pianikova made Alice the Fox and Basilio the Cat her heroes — in Igor Rogalyov’s apt words, “the violin was literally meowing in her hands”.
Julia Pianikova was among the competition laureates performing at the classical music concert of the 16th International Cultural Festival “Flowers of Russia” in Düsseldorf.

quotes.text: The soloists of the 12th Kogan-Fest gala concert, Julia Pianikova among them, won the audience over with their virtuosity, passion and extraordinary energy.
Julia Pianikova took first place at the International Kogan-Fest in Yaroslavl, winning over both the jury and the audience together with the other laureates.

quotes.text: The Setouchi International Music Festival programme features leading Japanese cellist Dai Miyata and Russian violinist Julia Pianikova.

A win at Kogan-Fest in Yaroslavl brought violinist Julia Pianikova to the stage in Japan: on 19 September she performed at the Setouchi International Music Festival, and on 14 November she will play the same programme at the Yaroslavl Philharmonic.
The Setouchi International Music Festival opened in Takamatsu, where first-class playing captivated an audience of 700.
The Setouchi International Music Festival in Kagawa Prefecture drew 2,200 listeners. Performers included cellist Dai Miyata and Russian violinist Julia Pianikova.
In September 2026 I was in Japan for the first time — and straight away at an event as large as the Setouchi International Music Festival 2026...
